title: Google's Gemma 4 answers from a TPU in orbit
dek: Google says its Project Suncatcher satellite generated a Gemma 4 response in orbit, an early milestone in testing whether data-center AI hardware can operate in space.
whatHappened: On October 30, 2026, Google reported that its Project Suncatcher prototype had generated a Gemma 4 response in orbit earlier that week.
A ground station sent a prompt requesting a space-themed haiku; the satellite returned the result while passing Svalbard, Norway.
Google calls it the first AI response from a data-center-class TPU in orbit; the prototype satellite launched on October 1.
Thermal-stress and radiation tests are next, ahead of a planned twin-satellite milestone in 2027.
whyItMatters: Executing an AI workload in orbit gives Google an initial operational test of the hardware behind its space-compute research.
take: Our view: this is a useful engineering milestone, not proof that orbital AI infrastructure is commercially viable.
openQuestions: The update does not establish long-term reliability, operating economics or commercial availability.
